verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verse.sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
verse.line: Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.
verse.translation: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
verse.why: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

matched.label: I want to reconnect with my roots

prasang.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, where Arjuna is paralyzed by doubt and guilt. Krishna tells him that to end this confusion, he must approach those who have seen the truth with humility, ask real questions, and serve them. This is not about blind obedience. It is about a willing posture that allows knowledge to actually enter and cut through doubt so he can act.
verse.for_you: You are ready to ask real questions and serve the process. Let your curiosity be the bow you lower to receive what you seek. The knowledge you need is already there.
verse.try_today: Notice where you feel humility when asking a question today.
verse.scene_line: You are on the edge of a battlefield, ready to lower your bow and ask.
asks: How do I approach this without feeling small?
Who in my life has seen the truth I need?
What does service look like when I am just learning?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse.sanskrit: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
verse.line: Dwell on something and you get attached; attachment becomes wanting, and blocked wanting turns into anger.
verse.translation: When a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.
verse.why: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

prasang.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

verse.meaning: Arjuna asks what a person of steady mind looks like. Krishna answers by describing someone who is content within and master of their senses. He then explains how a person loses this steadiness. When you dwell on something, attachment grows. From that attachment comes desire, and when that desire is blocked, it turns into anger and ruin.
verse.for_you: The Gita shows you that steadiness is built by guarding where your mind goes.
verse.try_today: Notice when your mind returns to your cousin's choice and let it rest there for a moment.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own waiting room, and the question is what you will dwell on.
asks: How do I guard my attention from anger?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
verse.sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
verse.line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
verse.translation: As the all-pervading sky, because of its subtlety, is not stained, so the self, present in every body, is not stained.
verse.why: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

prasang.title: Nature and spirit
prasang.summary: Nature does the acting; the self witnesses. Some reach the truth by meditation, some by reason, some by work, some by listening. Whoever sees the same divine in all beings stops harming themselves.
prasang.lesson: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

verse.meaning: Krishna is showing Arjuna the difference between the body and the spirit. He points to the sky, which remains clean no matter what moves through it. He tells Arjuna that the self is like that sky, present in every body yet untouched by what that body does. The self is not divided by birth or action. If you see the same presence in everyone, you stop wounding yourself with difference.
verse.for_you: You are trying to find the right words for your cousin, but the self does not divide. The same presence is in the girl your cousin wants, in your cousin, and in you.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you see the same presence in someone you judge different from you.
verse.scene_line: You stand between your cousin's choice and your family's worry, looking for a ground that birth cannot break.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verse.sanskrit: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥
verse.line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
verse.translation: One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and whose light is within, that yogi becomes one with Brahman and reaches the peace of Brahman.

words.en: becoming one with the supreme reality

verse.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

prasang.title: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna about the person who sees clearly. This person finds happiness inside, not in the world outside. Their joy and their light come from within themselves. Because of this, they become one with the deepest truth and reach a lasting peace.
verse.for_you: You are trying to sort out what the texts say about caste and marriage for your cousin. You want a clear answer you can stand on. The Gita points you away from birth and toward the self. Your own clarity is the ground you can stand on.
verse.try_today: Notice when your peace depends on someone else's approval or a specific outcome.
verse.scene_line: You are in the middle of a conversation where your peace feels like it is on the line.
asks: What does it mean to find my light within?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः । स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥
verse.line: Devoted to your own work, you reach fulfilment. Here's how.
verse.translation: Each person, devoted to his own work, attains perfection. Hear how one devoted to his own work finds perfection.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stay in the job your community or birth assigned'. 'Your own work' means the work that fits your nature.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is explaining how a person finds perfection through their own nature. He tells Arjuna that each person, devoted to their own work, attains perfection. The point is to do the work that fits your nature, flaws and all, as an offering. This does not mean staying in a job assigned by your community or birth. It means doing the work that fits your nature, as worship, and finding fulfilment there. The path that belongs to you, even if it has flaws, is better than another's.
verse.for_you: This verse asks you to look at your own work, not the work of your birth. Your cousin wants to marry a girl from a lower caste. The text says do the work that fits your nature.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment at work where you feel you are doing what fits your nature.
asks: How do I know what work fits my own nature?
What does it mean to do my work as an offering?
How do I explain this to my cousin?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna describes those whom he lifts out of the sea of mortality (12.7).
verse.sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥ तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥
verse.line: Lay your work in me and keep your mind on me; I soon lift you out of the drowning sea.
verse.translation: But those who lay all their actions in me, intent on me, and worship me meditating with single-minded yoga — for them, whose minds are set on me, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth, Partha.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, describing those who escape the cycle of death. He tells Arjuna that those who dedicate all their actions to him, focus their minds entirely, and worship him through steady, single-minded yoga, will be lifted out of the ocean of mortality. The teaching is that complete dedication of action and thought to the divine is the way to liberation.
verse.for_you: You are trying to find what the texts say about varna and marriage so you can speak to your cousin. You are looking for an answer that is clear and rooted.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you place your work or your mind in me, and see what that feels like.
verse.scene_line: You stand on the battlefield of your cousin's question, offering your mind to the text.
asks: How do I place my work in me when I am just trying to understand?
How does the text lift me out of the drowning sea of my cousin's question?

story.title: Arjuna asks to see the cosmic form
story.story_hook: His confusion gone, Arjuna made a bold request of his friend: show me who you really are.
story.summary: Thanking Krishna for dispelling his confusion, Arjuna asks to see his imperishable form if he is able.
story.lesson: Ask humbly for what you long to see.

story.hook_title: Arjuna asked his best friend Krishna to show who he really was
story.teaser: Arjuna asked his best friend Krishna to show who he really was
